title: (RHBA-2020:0641) Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage 4.2.2 Bug Fix update
portal_summary: Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage release 4.2.2 is now available with updates to packages and images that fix several bugs.
portal_synopsis: Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage 4.2.2 Bug Fix update
portal_product_filter: Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation|Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation|4|x86_64
portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

The Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage 4.2.2 container images provided by
this update can be downloaded from the Red Hat Container Registry at
registry.redhat.io. Installation instructions for your platform are
available at Red Hat Container Catalog.
portal_description:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage is software-defined storage integrated with and optimized for the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage is a highly scalable, production-grade persistent storage for stateful applications running in the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. In addition to persistent storage, Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage provisions a multicloud data management service with an S3 compatible API.

This updated advisory includes CVE fixes from Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 on sqlite, libarchive, and sudo.

This advisory also fixes the following bugs:

* Earlier, while working in a proxy environment, the NooBaa component used a local address of RGW which was not always available. Hence, the default backing store of OpenShift Container Storage was offline and the ocs-operator could not reach the "Ready" state. With this update, the cluser-wide address which is always available is used and the ocs-operator gets to a "Ready" state in a proxy environment. The default backing store created as expected. (BZ#1793189)

* Previously, monitoring agents tried to identify if public IP/DNS is available for NooBaa backing stores while behind a proxy or in a limited access environment. Hence, the monitoring of the backing stores fails as they are marked as offline and cannot be used. With this update, the limited wait time is included for an answer and then proceed to work normally even if no public IP/DNS is retrieved. With this fix, NooBaa backing stores operate normally in all environments. (BZ#1788520)

All Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage 4.2 users are advised to upgrade to these updated packages and images.
